prospect.name: Emanuel Solís
prospect.location: Madrid, Spain; originally from Mexico City. Holds both a Spanish and a US mobile number and describes the US one as his primary identity.
prospect.training_background: Started training around 28-29 and first got in shape at 30-31. Ten years of conventional gym work - three sets of twelve, isolation machines. Has bought several three- and six-month Instagram coaching programmes over the years and is now finishing a full year with an Instagram coach, during which he trained four to five times a week every week - the first sustained discipline of his life. Commutes 25 minutes each way to a less crowded gym. Does zero cardio. Has done restorative yoga in the past for stretching. No kettlebell work.
prospect.medical: No conditions, medications or injuries disclosed, and none beyond mobility were asked about. Reports intermittent sensations rather than pain in his left shoulder, left elbow and left knee after heavy sessions - 'it won't be pain, but I will feel the joint' - which he attributes to a decade of isolation training. Takes turmeric for joint health and says he generally enjoys good bone and joint health.

signals: Explicitly good-to-great and says so in those words: 'I no longer I'm seeking like a transformation. I think I already have experienced it'
Already fit - self-rates 7/10 on physique, can see his abs, has trained four to five times a week for twelve unbroken months
The blocker was proof, not price: 'it is hefty to pay that much up front without having any experience of the program' and 'I think I require some proof points in experience'
Highly self-directed and analytical - tracks macros with AI, has his own hypothesis about why he plateaued, articulates a ten-year plan for his body
Some overlap with skeptical_bargain_hunter in that he is anchored to a competing programme, but he never argued price level, only payment structure and risk

goals.text: Add 10-15 lb of muscle with broader, rounder shoulders, a bigger chest and more developed hamstrings
Get abs visible without flexing by shedding a little more fat
Build the mobility he knows he is missing and stop the shoulder, elbow and knee sensations getting worse with age
Set himself up for the next decade while testosterone and body function are still in a good place - 'I see my youth slipping away'
Maintain independence and quality of life into his 60s, 70s and 80s
Learn it once and own it forever rather than paying a coach indefinitely
Train at home when he wants, without commuting 25 minutes each way to an uncrowded gym or depending on specific machines
Break a training plateau by giving his body a genuinely new stimulus

pains.text: Muscle gain plateaued after two to three months of increased intake despite twelve months of unbroken discipline
A decade of isolated machine work has left him feeling his left shoulder, elbow and knee, which he expects to worsen with age
Knows he is missing mobility entirely and calls himself ignorant on it - it was absent from every programme he has bought
Paid a full year up front for a programme that did not deliver what he expected
Madrid gyms are so crowded he commutes 25 minutes each way, and bought programmes often need machines his gym does not have
Historically could only sustain three to six months before a month-long break and a slow restart
Sense of urgency about age - 42, watching a window close
Cannot physically eat any more food to push past 3,000 calories

objections.raw_quote: it is hefty to pay that much up front without having any experience of the program. So like, I wonder if, you know, it could be broken into three payments, you know, like 2,000 every two months. Or something like that, as to understand as I go the real value.
objections.rep_response: Isolated and diagnosed it well - 'is it more of a, I want to make sure I'm investing the right thing so I'm not blowing my money, or what is it sort of for you?' - confirming it was risk rather than affordability. Then stated flatly that the proposed structure was not available ('We don't do that') and improvised a one-month $1,200 trial with a walk-away right instead.

objections.raw_quote: Let me look at my numbers, but I can pay it between 2 and tomorrow... I just like to think about it.
objections.rep_response: Probed once - 'where's that coming from for you? Is it just making sure or what is it for you?' - and when the prospect declined to elaborate ('I don't need to elaborate on that. I think it's a choice that I have') the rep dropped it, said he was not applying pressure, and asked only for a completion date.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Rep rejected the prospect's proposed three payments of $2,000 every two months - 'We don't do that' - and offered two alternatives: split into three payments one month apart, or a $1,200 payment now acting as a one-month trial with a review meeting in three to four weeks and the right to walk away. If continuing, the balance would be 'two or three extra payments after that, and then it would stay 6,000'; the rep then added 'Otherwise, it would be six times 1,200', which totals $7,200. The discrepancy was never reconciled and the prospect responded 'Got it. That sounds interesting.'
offer.guarantee_mentioned: No formal guarantee. The nearest thing stated was the walk-away right on the trial: 'If you feel like I love this, then we keep going. If you feel like I hate it, we leave it.'

evidence: Clear verbal agreement to move forward: 'Perfect. And basically with this... I would say, let's get you started. Get you on board with Trevor?' 'Yeah, let's do it.'
Payment link sent in the chat and confirmed as working: 'That link that I sent in the chat, does that work?' 'Yes.'
Onboarding questionnaire sent on WhatsApp and confirmed received
Two follow-up meetings booked - an onboarding walkthrough the next day at 6pm and a review on Monday the 27th at 10:15pm

Counter-evidence, and it is real: no money changed hands on the call. Asked 'Can I get you started now?' he said 'Let me look at my numbers' and then 'I just like to think about it', committing only to paying by the following day
Further counter-evidence: what he agreed to is a $1,200 trial with an explicit right to walk away after a month, not a $6,000 commitment, and the total was left ambiguous between $6,000 and $7,200
outcome.cash_collection_basis: trial_instalment_committed_not_collected - $1,200 agreed for payment by the following day as a one-month trial; nothing was taken on the call and the full contract value was stated ambiguously as either $6,000 or six payments of $1,200
outcome.next_step: Prospect to pay $1,200 and complete the onboarding questionnaire by the next day; onboarding walkthrough call with the rep at 6pm the following day; trial review with the rep on Monday 27 July at 10:15pm Madrid time

notable.note: The rep invented a product on this call: a $1,200 one-month trial with an explicit right to walk away, offered after telling the prospect that his own proposed structure was not something Primal does. Two totals were then stated in consecutive sentences - $6,000 if he continues and pays in two or three further instalments, or 'six times 1,200' which is $7,200 - and the prospect said 'Got it' without either being clarified. Separately, this was the only call in the batch where explicit recording consent was requested and given, which is a credit to the rep and a contrast with the rest of the batch. Occupation was never asked at all, on a call that ended in a four-figure commitment.

quality.notes: Heavy inversion throughout, including at the two most commercially important moments: the price reveal at 00:45:37 ('we have an investment of 6k USD') is attributed to the prospect, and the payment-timing exchange from 00:54:17 to 00:54:58 alternates wrongly so that 'I just like to think about it' and 'I'm not pressuring you to do it' appear under the wrong speakers. The opening two lines are also inverted. Roles assigned from content throughout. The competing coach's name appears once as 'Brad Hills' but the surrounding text is garbled and the name should not be treated as reliable.
